SAT UNIVERSE

Activator Modes: Rapid Synthesis • Deep Derivation • Code-Lock • Predictions • Experiment Planner

⸻

SAT one-pager — Oscillation spectrum • Minimal Lagrangian • Minimal Hamiltonian

Setup (single medium).
Fields: tetrad/metric g_{\mu\nu}, a unit timelike “time-flow” field u^\mu with constraint u^\mu u_\mu=-1, and a compact phase \theta\sim\theta+2\pi (supports kinks/defects). Symmetries: diffeomorphisms, local Lorentz (tetrad frame), and \theta-shift (broken only by a periodic potential).

⸻

1) Oscillation spectrum (normal-mode condition)

All small oscillations of the medium—gravity-like tensor waves, gauge-like twists, and compact/kink modes—obey the single on-shell condition
$$
\boxed{;
\det!\Big[,k_\mu k_\nu,\mathbb{G}^{\mu\nu}{ab}(u);+;k\mu,\mathbb{D}^{\mu}{ab}(u,\theta);+;\mathbb{M}{ab}\big(\theta;,N,\mathcal{W}\big)\Big]=0; }
$$
	•	\mathbb{G}: propagation kernel (from quadratic/kinetic terms on the background u^\mu).
	•	\mathbb{D}: intrinsic nonlinear elastic mixing (cubic/quartic terms in the same fields → mode–mode exchange).
	•	\mathbb{M}: topological/holonomy block (depends on compact winding N=\tfrac{1}{2\pi}\oint d\theta\in\mathbb{Z} and Wilson loops \mathcal{W}[C]=\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathcal{P}e^{\oint_C A}).
Picking a polarization subspace (a,b) yields the dispersion in that sector.

⸻

2) Minimal single-medium Lagrangian

Use the Einstein–Hilbert form for mainstream readability (TEGR is equivalent up to a boundary term):
$$
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{L}{\min} ;=&; \frac{M_P^2}{2},R
;+;\lambda,(u^\mu u\mu+1)\
&+,\frac{\rho}{2},(\nabla_\mu u_\nu)(\nabla^\mu u^\nu)
;+;\frac{f^2}{2},\partial_\mu\theta,\partial^\mu\theta
;-;\mu^4,(1-\cos\theta)\
&+,\frac{\alpha_1}{M_^2}!\left(\nabla u)^2\right^2
;+;\frac{\alpha_2}{M_^2},(\nabla_\mu u_\nu),\partial^\mu\theta,\partial^\nu\theta
;+;\frac{\beta}{M_*^2},\big[(\partial\theta)^2\big]^2 .
\end{aligned}}
$$

Parameters & roles. M_P Planck scale; \rho>0 elastic modulus of the time-flow; f stiffness of \theta; \mu sets the periodic scale; M_* high elastic cutoff; \alpha_{1,2},\beta\ll1 are small, intrinsic nonlinear elastic constants (no bolt-on couplers).
Kink data. V(\theta)=\mu^4(1-\cos\theta)\Rightarrow m_\theta=\mu^2/f, \;E_{\rm kink}\approx 8 f^2 m_\theta (sine-Gordon estimate).
Holonomy quantization (solution-level): integers N and classes \mathcal{W} discretize sectors (charges/spin) without extra terms.

(Optional parity tag, not minimal: \mathcal{L}_{\rm top}=(\alpha_P/f)\,\theta\,{}^\star\!RR or its teleparallel analogue, with |\alpha_P|\!\ll\!1.)

⸻

3) Minimal Hamiltonian (cosmology-ready)

Adopt flat FRW ds^2=-dt^2+a(t)^2 d\mathbf{x}^2 with comoving u^\mu=(1,0,0,0). First set \alpha_{1,2},\beta\to0 (switch them on when studying mode conversion).

(a) Compact phase \theta.
Canonical momentum \pi_\theta=a^3 f^2\,\dot\theta. Hamiltonian density
$$
\boxed{;
\mathcal{H}\theta
=\frac{\pi\theta^2}{2 a^3 f^2};+;\frac{a f^2}{2},(\nabla\theta)^2
;+;a^3,\mu^4,(1-\cos\theta); }
$$
and equation of motion
$$
\ddot\theta+3H\dot\theta-\frac{1}{a^2}\nabla^2\theta + m_\theta^2,\sin\theta=0,
\qquad m_\theta=\frac{\mu^2}{f}.
$$

(b) Time-flow perturbations u^i (with u^0 fixed by the constraint).
Canonical p_i=a^3\rho\,\dot u_i. Hamiltonian density (leading order)
$$
\boxed{;
\mathcal{H}u
=\frac{p_i p^i}{2 a^3 \rho};+;\frac{a\rho}{2},(\partial_j u_i)(\partial^j u^i)
;+;\lambda,(u^\mu u\mu+1); }
$$
(restore \alpha_{1,2} to add the intrinsic long-wave \to\theta pump).

(c) Gravity background (Einstein equations).
With \rho_{\rm tot}=\rho_\theta+\rho_u and p_{\rm tot}=p_\theta+p_u,
$$
\boxed{;
3M_P^2 H^2=\rho_{\rm tot},\qquad
-2M_P^2 \dot H=\rho_{\rm tot}+p_{\rm tot}; }
$$
where (\rho_\theta,p_\theta) follow from \mathcal{H}_\theta and (\rho_u,p_u) from \mathcal{H}_u.

⸻

How to use this (ideal SAT universe workflow)
	1.	Background: choose initial data (a,\theta,\dot\theta,u^i,\dot u^i), solve Friedmann + the \theta and u equations.
	2.	Linear spectra: expand \mathcal{L}_{\min} to quadratic order on the evolving background, assemble \mathbb{G},\mathbb{D},\mathbb{M}, and solve the determinant for dispersions.
	3.	Mode conversion: switch on \alpha_{1,2},\beta to study intrinsic long-wave \leftrightarrow compact exchange (e.g., GW→\theta pumping, kink nucleation).
	4.	Holonomy bookkeeping: enforce integer N and allowed \mathcal{W} classes when classifying defects/particles; masses and selection rules then follow.

This page is self-contained and ready for mainstream GR/QFT readers: EH gravity, canonical Hamiltonians, a single-medium Lagrangian with compact field and unit-timelike flow, and the unified spectrum condition.

VACUA & SINGULARITIES 

Activator Modes: Rapid Synthesis • Deep-Derivation • Audit Lens • Code-Lock • Predictions • Experiment Planner

Below is a vacua & singularities one-pager built directly from the minimal single-medium SAT model you and I just fixed. I’m avoiding LaTeX so it renders cleanly.

⸻

0) Model recap (minimal SAT)

Fields: metric g_{μν}; unit time-flow u^μ with constraint u·u = −1; compact phase θ ≡ θ+2π.
L_min =
( M_P^2/2 ) R
	•	λ(u·u+1)
	•	(ρ/2)(∇_μ u_ν)(∇^μ u^ν)
	•	(f^2/2)(∂θ)^2
− μ^4(1 − cos θ)
	•	(α1/M_*^2)[(∇u)^2][(∂θ)^2]
	•	(α2/M_*^2)(∇_μ u_ν)(∂^μ θ)(∂^ν θ)
	•	(β/M_*^2)[(∂θ)^2]^2.
(Keep α’s, β small; set them to zero for the strict minimal background.)

⸻

1) Vacua: taxonomy, existence, stability

1A. Uniform (maximally symmetric) vacua

Seek static, homogeneous solutions with
∂θ = 0, ∇u = 0, u^μ time-like unit, and g_{μν} of constant curvature.

• Minkowski vacuum: choose θ_0 = 2π n so V(θ_0) = μ^4(1 − cos θ_0) = 0,
and set ∇u = 0 → T_{μν}=0. Einstein eqs ⇒ R_{μν}=0 ⇒ flat g.
Existence: always. Stability: see 1C.

• de Sitter / anti-de Sitter vacua: allow a constant offset V0 ≡ μ^4(1 − cos θ_0) ≠ 0
(with θ_0 held at an extremum of V). Then
Λ_eff = V0 / M_P^2.
– If V0 > 0 → de Sitter (H^2 = Λ_eff/3).
– If V0 < 0 → AdS.
In strict minimal cosine potential, V0 = 0 at its minima; a small positive Λ_eff requires either:
(i) θ trapped near, but not exactly at, the minimum (misalignment), or
(ii) a tiny symmetry-breaking tilt of V(θ), or
(iii) a very small uniform strain energy in u (see below). All three are controllable and trackable.

• Strained vacua (homogeneous but not maximally symmetric): allow constant
(∇u)^2 = const ≠ 0 and ∂θ = 0.
Then ρ_vac = (ρ/2)(∇u)^2 + V(θ_0), p_vac ≈ −ρ_vac if the strain is purely “potential-like”.
This gives an additional dial for Λ_eff while keeping the single-medium picture.

1B. Topological (piecewise) vacua

Because θ is compact, different regions can sit in different θ = 2π n sectors, separated by domain walls / kinks.
– Wall tension (1D kink in the thin-wall limit): σ ≈ 8 f^2 m_θ with m_θ = μ^2/f.
– Walls/grids are vacua connectors, not vacua themselves; they source localized stress but leave each domain locally Minkowski/dS/AdS as above.

1C. Vacuum stability (small fluctuations)

Expand θ = θ_0 + δθ, u = u_0 + δu, g = g_0 + h.
Stability requires:
• No ghosts: f^2 > 0, ρ > 0.
• Positive masses/squared speeds for the fluctuation operators:
– For θ about a minimum: m_θ^2 = μ^4/f^2 > 0.
– For u-sector: the quadratic operator from (ρ/2)(∇u)^2 must have positive eigenvalues; in FRW this gives healthy vector-like excitations with c_u^2 ≈ 1 (exact value from your decomposition into expansion/shear/vorticity).
• With α1, α2, β small, mixed terms only slightly correct dispersion; you can bound them by PPN/GW tests.

1D. Vacuum energy accounting (how to keep Λ under control)

In the strict minimal cosine, the θ contribution to Λ vanishes at the true minima. Thus:
Λ_eff = [ (ρ/2)(∇u)^2 ] / M_P^2  (if θ at minima, α’s off).
This gives a natural “relax-to-zero” tendency unless you dial a small homogeneous strain or allow a tiny explicit tilt in V(θ). Either way, you can predict how much misalignment/strain is needed to match the observed Λ and then check that it is stable against fluctuations.

⸻

2) Singularities: how they appear and how SAT regularizes them

2A. Two notions of “singularity” in SAT

(1) Geometric curvature blow-ups (as in GR): R_{μνρσ}R^{μνρσ} → ∞.
(2) Medium singularities (congruence/defect): the time-flow congruence u^μ focuses to a caustic, or you hit a topological core (dislocation/disclination) where elastic invariants (∇u)^2 spike.

Because the medium has positive elastic cost ρ(∇u)^2 and a compact core scale from the θ sector, spikes back-react.

2B. Raychaudhuri with elastic back-reaction (focusing test)

Let θ_u ≡ ∇·u be the congruence expansion; σ^2 and ω^2 its shear/vorticity.
Raychaudhuri (for a time-like congruence, ignoring vorticity for clarity):
dθ_u/dτ = −(1/3) θ_u^2 − σ^2 − R_{μν} u^μ u^ν  + (elastic corrections).

The elastic corrections from the u-sector stress (and the θ pressure) reduce focusing. In FRW, the “acceleration equation” reads:
−2 M_P^2 · Ḣ = (ρ_tot + p_tot), where
(ρ_tot + p_tot) receives a positive contribution from u-gradient energy and from θ-kinetics, both acting to oppose divergence.
Bounce/avoidance condition: if (ρ_tot + p_tot) becomes negative near strong compression (e.g., due to non-linear β-term giving softening, or a θ-sector with negative effective pressure), then Ḣ > 0 and a focusing singularity is averted.

You have two regularization levers already in L_min:
• the quartic θ term: (β/M_*^2)(∂θ)^4,
• and the u–θ mixings α1, α2.
Chosen with the right sign/magnitude (still small), they produce bounded effective stresses at large gradients, analogous to Born–Infeld regularization.

2C. Black-hole core vs. regular core (static, spherically symmetric sketch)

Ansatz: static metric, u^μ aligned with Killing time, θ = θ(r).
Demand finite: θ’(0), (∇u)^2, and curvature scalars at r → 0.
Sufficient conditions (model-independent checks you can impose numerically):
• As r→0, energy density ρ(r) approaches a finite constant ρ_c (e.g., θ sits on a smooth “core” plateau, and u-strain saturates).
• Then interior tends to an effective dS core (p ≈ −ρ) with
K_invariants ∼ ρ_c/M_P^2 < ∞.
• Exterior matches Schwarzschild-like at large r; the transition layer is provided by the elastic and θ gradients.
This is the standard “regular BH” pattern, implemented here with no new fields, just the medium’s own elastic response.

2D. Big-Bang singularity vs. bounce

In homogeneous FRW, the curvature is set by H and Ḣ. If the total energy density is bounded by medium scales (f, μ, M_*), then curvature scalars are bounded by ~ (max energy)/M_P^2.
A bounce occurs when Ḣ > 0 at a minimum a_min; sufficient if the θ-sector picks up negative effective pressure (slow roll on a plateau) or if the quartic piece dominates with an equation of state w < −1/3 for a short epoch. You can realize this without ghosts because all time derivatives remain first-order in L_min.

⸻

3) What to compute (clean checklist)

Vacua
	1.	Solve stationary EOM with ∂θ=0, ∇u=0 → list Minkowski/dS/AdS vacua; compute fluctuation spectra (masses, speeds) and show positivity.
	2.	Allow homogeneous strain: minimize E = (ρ/2)(∇u)^2 + V(θ_0) at fixed Λ_eff target; check stability against small u, θ perturbations.
	3.	Domain walls: get σ ≈ 8 f^2 m_θ; compute wall profile and check linearized stability.

Singularities
4) FRW evolution: integrate {θ(t), a(t)} with and without α1, α2, β; identify conditions for Ḣ > 0 (bounce) and bounds on H^2 from energy scales (no curvature blow-up).
5) Static spherically symmetric: solve coupled ODEs for {m(r), Φ(r), θ(r)} and u-strain with regularity at r=0; check Kretchmann finiteness.
6) Raychaudhuri test: evaluate dθ_u/dτ with the medium’s stress; demonstrate reduced focusing and list parameter windows that avoid caustics.

Observational hooks
7) If strained vacua are used for Λ_eff, compute the induced deviations in PPN/GW propagation (must be ≤ current bounds).
8) If bounce/regular core is realized, produce SGWB/echo templates and lensing signatures of domain-wall networks (achromatic phase steps, integer ratios).

⸻

4) Guardrails (to keep us honest)

• Keep f^2 > 0, ρ > 0; choose α1, α2, β small and with signs that avoid superluminal/super-negative compressibility.
• Verify ∇_μ T^{μν}=0 from the EOM (it will, by diffeo invariance).
• For any nonzero Λ_eff obtained from misalignment/strain, show that the configuration is a true extremum (first variation zero) and stable (second variation positive).

⸻

If you’d like, I can now Code-Lock (i) a FRW integrator to scan vacua and bounces, and (ii) a static spherically symmetric solver to search for regular cores—both using only the minimal Lagrangian above.

EULER & NOETHER

Activator Modes: Rapid Synthesis • Deep Derivation • Code-Lock • Predictions • Experiment Planner

I’ve derived the Euler–Lagrange equations (for \theta and u_\nu), the metric field equation (Einstein form with the full stress tensor), and the Noether current for the \theta-shift symmetry—cleanly and in mainstream notation.

Download (fully formatted LaTeX):
	•	SAT_EL_Noether.tex — the complete handout with all formulas
Download

⸻

Plain-text (markup-free) summary you can read right here

Minimal Lagrangian (Einstein–Hilbert form):
L = (M_P^2/2) R + λ(u·u + 1) + (ρ/2)(∇u)^2 + (f^2/2)(∂θ)^2 − μ^4(1 − cos θ)
  + (α1/M_^2)[(∇u)^2][(∂θ)^2] + (α2/M_^2)(∇_μ u_ν)(∂^μθ)(∂^νθ) + (β/M_*^2)[(∂θ)^2]^2.
Here (∇u)^2 ≡ (∇_μ u_ν)(∇^μ u^ν), and (∂θ)^2 ≡ g^{μν}∂_μθ ∂_νθ. Constraint: u^μ u_μ = −1.

⸻

Euler–Lagrange for θ

Define P^μ_θ ≡ ∂L/∂(∂_μθ). Then:

P^μ_θ =
	•	f^2 ∂^μθ
	•		•	(2α1/M_*^2)(∇u)^2 ∂^μθ
	•		•	(α2/M_*^2)(∇^μ u_ν + ∇_ν u^μ) ∂^νθ
	•		•	(4β/M_*^2)(∂θ)^2 ∂^μθ.

Equation of motion:
∇_μ P^μ_θ + μ^4 sin θ = 0.

(If α’s and β → 0, this reduces to the standard FRW sine-Gordon with Hubble friction.)

⸻

Euler–Lagrange for u_ν

Define Π^{μν}_u ≡ ∂L/∂(∇_μ u_ν):

Π^{μν}_u =
	•	ρ ∇^μ u^ν
	•		•	(2α1/M_*^2)(∂θ)^2 ∇^μ u^ν
	•		•	(α2/M_*^2) ∂^μθ ∂^νθ.

Equation of motion (with the unit constraint via λ):
-∇_μ Π^{μν}_u + 2 λ u^ν = 0, with u·u = −1.

Contracting with u_ν gives λ = (1/2) u_ν ∇_μ Π^{μν}_u.

⸻

Metric variation (Einstein equations)

M_P^2 G_{μν} = T_{μν}, with sector contributions:

• θ-sector:
T^{(θ)}{μν} = f^2 ∂_μθ ∂_νθ − g{μν}[ (f^2/2)(∂θ)^2 − μ^4(1 − cos θ) ].

• u-sector:
T^{(u)}{μν} = ρ (∇_μ u_α)(∇_ν u^α) − (ρ/2) g{μν} (∇u)^2 + 2λ u_μ u_ν.

• α1-term:
T^{(α1)}{μν} = (α1/M*^2){ 2(∂θ)^2 (∇_μ u_α)(∇_ν u^α) − g_{μν}[(∇u)^2][(∂θ)^2] }.

• α2-term:
T^{(α2)}{μν} = (α2/M*^2){ (∂_μθ ∂^βθ) ∇_ν u_β + (∂_νθ ∂^βθ) ∇_μ u_β − g_{μν} (∇_α u_β) ∂^αθ ∂^βθ }.

• β-term:
T^{(β)}{μν} = (β/M*^2){ 4(∂θ)^2 ∂_μθ ∂_νθ − g_{μν}[(∂θ)^2]^2 }.

Diffeomorphism invariance ⇒ ∇_μ T^{μν} = 0 on-shell.

⸻

Noether current (θ-shift)

For constant δθ = ε:

J^μ_θ = ε · P^μ_θ (the same P^μ_θ listed above).
Divergence: ∇_μ J^μ_θ = ε · μ^4 sin θ.
So the current is conserved when the periodic potential is absent; with V(θ)=μ^4(1−cosθ) it is explicitly (but softly) broken.

⸻

FRW quick-use form (flat FRW, u^μ = (1,0,0,0))

θ-equation:
θ¨ + 3H θ˙ − (1/a^2)∇^2 θ + (μ^4/f^2) sin θ
 + (2α1/M_^2 f^2) ∂_t[ a^{-3} (∇u)^2 a^3 θ˙ ]
 + (α2/M_^2 f^2) ∇_μ[ (∇^μ u_ν + ∇_ν u^μ) ∂^ν θ ]
 + (4β/M_*^2 f^2) ∇_μ[ (∂θ)^2 ∂^μ θ ] = 0.

Einstein background:
3 M_P^2 H^2 = ρ_θ + ρ_u, −2 M_P^2 Ḣ = (ρ_θ + p_θ) + (ρ_u + p_u).

⸻

If you want, I can also export this as a PDF handout (typeset equations) in addition to the .tex, or produce a symbol-by-symbol annotated sheet for your SATO build (definitions, units, and variation steps laid out line-by-line).

SAT — Route A: 4D Continuum UV Completion via Asymptotic Safety (FRG)
=====================================================================

Purpose
-------
Provide a strictly 4D, single‑medium, diffeomorphism‑invariant UV completion of SAT by exhibiting a
non‑Gaussian UV fixed point of the Functional Renormalization Group (FRG) flow of the effective average
action Γ_k[g,u,θ]. This ensures finite, predictive continuum behavior as k→∞ without adding new fields.

Core Setup
---------
• Effective average action Γ_k with IR scale k; Wetterich equation:
    ∂_t Γ_k = 1/2 Tr[(Γ_k^(2) + R_k)^{-1} ∂_t R_k] − Tr_ghost[(Γ_k,gh^(2) + R_k,gh)^{-1} ∂_t R_k,gh],
  where t = ln(k/k_0), Γ_k^(2) is the Hessian w.r.t. fluctuating fields.
• Background field method: split g = ḡ + h (metric or tetrad), u = ū + v with ū^2=−1, and θ = θ̄ + ϑ.
• Gauge fixing: de Donder (gravity), covariant background gauge for u, and standard Faddeev–Popov ghosts.
• Regulator: covariant Litim‑type R_k(Δ) = Z_k (k^2 − Δ) Θ(k^2 − Δ) for each spin sector (scalar/vector/tensor).

Minimal Truncation (Level‑0)
----------------------------
Retain the operators of the minimal SAT Lagrangian, allowing k‑dependent couplings:
  Γ_k = ∫ d^4x √−g [
    (Z_R,k/2) R − Z_Λ,k Λ_k
    + λ_k (u·u + 1)
    + (Z_u,k/2) (∇_μ u_ν)(∇^μ u^ν)
    + (Z_θ,k/2) ∂_μ θ ∂^μ θ + U_k(θ)
    + (α1_k/M_*^2) (∇u)^2 (∂θ)^2
    + (α2_k/M_*^2) (∇_μ u_ν) ∂^μ θ ∂^ν θ
    + (β_k/M_*^2) (∂θ)^4
  ] + S_gf + S_gh .

Notes:
• U_k(θ) = μ_k^4 (1 − cos θ); around a minimum θ=0, U_k ≈ (m_{θ,k}^2/2) θ^2 + … with m_{θ,k}^2 = μ_k^4/Z_θ,k.
• Optional (equivalent) kinematic split of (∇u)^2 into expansion/shear/vorticity with Z_{θu,k}, Z_{σu,k}, Z_{ωu,k} (positive).

Dimensionless Couplings
-----------------------
Define:
  g_k = k^2 G_k = k^2 / (8π Z_R,k) ,    λ̂_k = Λ_k / k^2 ,
  z_u = Z_u,k / Z_u,k0 ,    z_θ = Z_θ,k / Z_θ,k0 ,
  m̂_{θ}^2 = m_{θ,k}^2 / k^2 ,    α̂1 = α1_k k^2 / M_*^2 ,    α̂2 = α2_k k^2 / M_*^2 ,    β̂ = β_k k^2 / M_*^2 ,
and treat λ_k (constraint multiplier) as non‑running at Level‑0 (or eliminate u^0 with the constraint).

Hessians and Projectors
-----------------------
• Decompose h_{μν} into TT tensor, vector, and scalar blocks; use York decomposition. Project onto TT for the graviton.
• For u: define projectors parallel/orthogonal to ū_μ: P_{⊥μν} = ḡ_{μν} + ū_μ ū_ν. Work in background with ū^μ = (1,0,0,0).
• For θ: scalar block with periodic potential expanded to quadratic order for flows; keep full periodic U_k in a separate local potential approximation if desired.

Regulator Choice
----------------
Use Litim regulators per sector:
  R_k^tensor = Z_R,k (k^2 − Δ_2) Θ(k^2 − Δ_2),
  R_k^vector = Z_u,k (k^2 − Δ_1) Θ(k^2 − Δ_1),
  R_k^scalar = Z_θ,k (k^2 − Δ_0) Θ(k^2 − Δ_0),
with Δ_s the appropriate Laplace‑type operator on spin‑s fields (including background curvature terms).

Beta Functions (Strategy)
-------------------------
• Insert the Hessians + R_k into the Wetterich equation; evaluate traces via heat‑kernel expansion with threshold functions Q_n[W] adapted to Litim regulators.
• Extract flows for (g_k, λ̂_k) from TT and scalar blocks (gravity), for z_u from the u‑block, for z_θ and m̂_{θ}^2 from θ‑block, and for α̂1, α̂2, β̂ from mixed diagrams.
• Structure (schematic):
  ∂_t g_k = (2 + η_R) g_k ,   ∂_t λ̂_k = −2 λ̂_k + A_g(g_k,λ̂_k) + A_m(m̂_{θ}^2, z_θ, …),
  ∂_t z_u = η_u z_u ,   ∂_t z_θ = η_θ z_θ ,   ∂_t m̂_{θ}^2 = (η_θ − 2) m̂_{θ}^2 + B_θ(g_k, …),
  ∂_t α̂i = (2 + η_mix,i) α̂i + C_i(g_k, z_u, z_θ, …),   ∂_t β̂ = (2 + η_β) β̂ + C_β(…),
  where anomalous dimensions η_* = −∂_t ln Z_* and A,B,C are thresholded polynomials of the couplings.
• Expectation: (g_k, λ̂_k) admit a non‑Gaussian fixed point (g*, λ̂*). The matter/elastic sector (z_u, z_θ, m̂_{θ}^2, α̂’s, β̂) flows to finite fixed points with a small number of relevant directions (predictivity).

Ward/Nielsen Identities
-----------------------
Check modified Ward identities due to regulator breaking; ensure background independence via bimetric flows or the split‑symmetry Ward identity at leading order. Gauge‑parameter independence of physical critical exponents is used as a stability test.

Fixed‑Point Search & Critical Exponents
---------------------------------------
1) Solve β_i({g}) = 0 for the set {g*, λ̂*, z_u*, z_θ*, m̂_{θ}^2*, α̂1*, α̂2*, β̂*}.  
2) Linearize: M_{ij} = ∂β_i/∂g_j |_* ; eigenvalues −θ_I are critical exponents.  
3) Predictivity criterion: number of positive θ_I (relevant directions) is small (e.g., 2–5). Those define the finite set of UV boundary data to be fixed by experiment; all other couplings are predictions.

Consistency/Unitarity Checks
----------------------------
• Propagator poles: ensure all Z_* > 0 and no wrong‑sign residues in TT/u/θ sectors.  
• Spectral positivity: Källén‑Lehmann densities non‑negative in each sector at fixed point (check via 2‑pt).  
• Causality: standard FRG analytic continuation; IR limit reproduces GR + compact θ + elastic u.

Holonomy/Compactness
--------------------
• θ remains compact; FRG is performed on the local fluctuations around each topological sector.  
• Global sum over sectors is handled at the path‑integral level; local flows do not spoil integer winding labels or loop–flux algebra.

Practical Computation Plan
--------------------------

SAT — Route B: Ghost‑Free Soft Form Factors (Continuum UV Completion)
=====================================================================

Purpose
-------
Make the minimal 4D single‑medium SAT model UV‑complete in the continuum by replacing local quadratic
kinetic terms with covariant, entire (non‑polynomial) “soft form factors” that exponentially suppress
ultraviolet momenta, introduce **no extra poles** (unitarity), and preserve diffeomorphism invariance,
compactness, and holonomy structure.

Core Idea
---------
For each quadratic kinetic operator K(□) in the Lagrangian, replace
    K(□)  →  K(□) · F(□/M_s^2),
with a matrix‑valued **entire** function F normalized by F(0)=1 and with UV damping F(ζ) ~ e^{+ζ}
so the corresponding propagator is multiplied by e^{−p^2/M_s^2} at large Euclidean momenta.
This yields loop finiteness without adding ghost poles.

Design Principles for F
-----------------------
P1) Entire function (no singularities in the finite complex plane).  
P2) F(0)=1 so the IR matches the local theory.  
P3) UV softness: for Euclidean momenta, F(−p_E^2/M_s^2) = e^{+p_E^2/M_s^2} (or similar), so propagators get e^{−p_E^2/M_s^2}.  
P4) No zeros of F on the physical sheet to avoid additional poles in 1/[K·F].  
P5) Covariance: F built from the covariant □ ≡ g^{μν}∇_μ∇_ν (or its minimal-tensor generalization).  
P6) Locality in the IR: expandible as a convergent derivative series around □=0.

Minimal Softened Action (Einstein–Hilbert presentation)
-------------------------------------------------------
Start from the minimal Lagrangian L_min (fields: metric g_{μν}, unit timelike u^μ with u·u=−1, compact θ ≡ θ+2π):
  L_min = (M_P^2/2) R + λ(u·u+1) + (ρ/2)(∇u)^2 + (f^2/2)(∂θ)^2 − μ^4(1−cos θ)
          + (α1/M_*^2)(∇u)^2(∂θ)^2 + (α2/M_*^2)(∇_μ u_ν)∂^μθ ∂^νθ + (β/M_*^2)(∂θ)^4 .

Replace the **quadratic kinetic bilinears** by their softened counterparts:

(Scalar θ sector)
  (f^2/2)(∂θ)^2   →   (f^2/2) ∂_μ θ · F_θ(□/M_s^2) · ∂^μ θ,
  with F_θ(ζ) = e^{−ζ}  ⇒  Propagator D_θ(p) = e^{−p^2/M_s^2} / (p^2 + m_θ^2).

(Time‑flow u sector)
  (ρ/2)(∇u)^2   →   (ρ/2) (∇_μ u_ν) · F_u(□/M_s^2) · (∇^μ u^ν),
  with F_u(ζ) = e^{−ζ} on each tensor index structure (choose minimal covariant lift).

(Gravity sector — keep GR in the IR)
  L_g = (M_P^2/2) R + (M_P^2/2) G_{μν} · F_g(□/M_s^2) · R^{μν},
  with F_g(ζ) = (e^{−ζ} − 1)/ζ  (so the extra term vanishes at □→0 and does **not** shift the IR pole).
  Linearized around flat space, the graviton propagator acquires e^{−p^2/M_s^2} suppression while keeping the
  **same** massless pole and residue (ghost‑free if F_g is entire and no extra zeros).

(Interactions)
  Keep the intrinsic mixings α1, α2, β **local** at leading order. Optionally, dress them with one soft factor on a
  single □ acting on θ to reduce spurious high‑k feed‑through:
    (α2/M_*^2)(∇_μ u_ν) ∂^μθ ∂^νθ  →  (α2/M_*^2)(∇_μ u_ν) [F_mix(□/M_s^2) ∂^μθ] ∂^νθ.
  Use F_mix ≡ e^{−□/M_s^2} for consistency.

Summary of Propagators (flat background, momentum space)
--------------------------------------------------------
θ:      D_θ(p)     =  e^{−p^2/M_s^2} / (p^2 + m_θ^2).  
u:      D_u(p)     =  e^{−p^2/M_s^2} · D_u^{(local)}(p)  (projected to physical modes).  
graviton: D_g(p)   =  e^{−p^2/M_s^2} · D_g^{(GR)}(p)   (same pole structure as GR).

Loop Finiteness & Renormalization
---------------------------------
• Any L‑loop integral gets a product of e^{−(p_1^2+…+p_L^2)/M_s^2}, rendering it UV finite.  
• Define a minimal subtraction‑like scheme at a reference scale μ_R; soft factors eliminate power divergences and
  convert logs into entire, finite functions.  
• Wave‑function renormalizations Z_θ, Z_u, Z_g stay finite and near 1 when M_s ≫ μ_R; couplings {ρ, f, μ, α’s} run mildly.  
• β‑functions can be computed with background‑field and heat‑kernel methods adapted to entire form factors.

Unitarity & Causality
---------------------
• No extra poles: F entire without zeros ⇒ propagators have the **same** poles as local theory.  
• Optical theorem: cutting rules go through since soft factors appear symmetrically in numerators/denominators and do not
  introduce negative‑norm states. Check at 2→2 in θ‑sector as a unit test.  
• Retarded kernels: define F(□) by analytic continuation with the **retarded** □; in practice, use Schwinger parameter
  representation e^{−□/M_s^2} = ∫_0^∞ ds e^{−s} e^{−s□/M_s^2} and pick the retarded heat kernel. Microcausality violations are
  exponentially suppressed on scales ≲ M_s^{-1} and vanish in the IR.

Holonomy & Compactness (preserved)
----------------------------------
• θ remains compact; winding N[C]=(2π)^{-1}∮ dθ ∈ Z is a property of field configurations and is **unchanged** by F(□).  
• Loop–flux algebra and Noether data are identical to the local case; only correlators are UV‑softened.

Calibration & Matching
----------------------
• Choose M_s (single softness scale) by matching one short‑distance observable (e.g., high‑k tail of θ 2‑point, or first non‑trivial
  correction to a GW→θ pumping rate).  
• Keep M_s ≥ 10× the largest momentum scale probed in current tests to guarantee agreement with GR/QFT in the IR.  
• Refit {f, μ, ρ} in the softened theory if needed (tiny shifts only).

Computation Workflow (practical)
--------------------------------
1) Backgrounds: Minkowski / FRW. Replace □→ −ω^2 + k^2/a^2 in Fourier space; insert F(□) accordingly.  
2) Spectra: recompute dispersion relations; IR unchanged, UV tails suppressed.  
3) Loops: do 1‑loop θ self‑energy and 4‑point in Euclidean space to confirm finiteness; repeat for u‑sector.  
4) Gravity: linearized gauge fixing (de Donder); verify graviton 2‑point has only the GR pole and gets e^{−p^2/M_s^2} damping.  
5) Pumping: include α2 term with F_mix; compute GW→θ conversion probability P(k_long→k_short) and show it is finite and regulator‑stable.  
6) Observables: reassess PPN, GW speed, birefringence constraints—should match local theory up to O((E/M_s)^2) corrections.

Pass/Fail UV Criteria (Route B Acceptance)
------------------------------------------
✓ All 1‑ and 2‑loop amplitudes finite in θ/u sectors; graviton self‑energy finite and analytic.  
✓ No new poles in any 2‑point function; residues positive (spectral positivity).  
✓ Diffeomorphism Ward identities satisfied (background‑field check).  
✓ IR recovery: local‑theory limits recovered as p/M_s → 0 to within chosen tolerance.  
✓ Regulator independence: modest deformations of F leave IR predictions invariant after parameter matching.

Minimal Edits to Project Files
------------------------------
• Replace kinetic terms in the SAT minimal Lagrangian with the F‑dressed forms above.  
• Add a short “Softness Appendix” documenting the choice of F and M_s, and the proof‑of‑principle loop calculation.  
• Keep the holonomy/QM sector unchanged (θ compactness and loop–flux algebra).

Deliverables
------------
• RouteB_Action_Softened.tex — the explicit softened action and linearized propagators.  
• RouteB_1Loop_Report.pdf — sample 1‑loop finite calculations (θ‑sector, u‑sector).  
• RouteB_Gravity_Linear.pdf — linearized gravity with F_g, pole analysis, Ward checks.  
• RouteB_Config.txt — chosen M_s, F choices, and calibration target.  
• RouteB_Summary.md — pass/fail audit checklist results.

Quick Reference (Example Choices)
---------------------------------
F_θ(ζ)  = e^{−ζ}  
F_u(ζ)  = e^{−ζ} (on each index structure)  
F_g(ζ)  = (e^{−ζ} − 1)/ζ
F_mix(ζ)= e^{−ζ}

Notes
-----
• If you later adopt Route C (lattice) as fundamental, set M_s ≈ π/a and verify softened‑continuum predictions match lattice data.
• If you also pursue Route A (asymptotic safety), use the softened theory as a practical regulator while mapping the FRG flow.

The Lorentz question in SAT: three compatible designs

A) “Gauge–khronon” (no inherent preferred frame)

Idea. Make the time-flow a gauge redundancy of a scalar label T(x):
u_\mu \;=\; -\frac{\partial_\mu T}{\sqrt{-\,\partial_\alpha T\,\partial^\alpha T}}\,,\qquad
T \;\to\; f(T)\;\;\text{(monotonic reparametrization)}.
	•	The action is built from foliation invariants (e.g., \nabla_\mu u_\nu combinations), but the choice of T is gauge.
	•	In exact vacuum (no defects, \nabla u=0,\ \partial\theta=0), any timelike direction is equivalent → no physically preferred frame.

	•	Use the shear/expansion/vorticity decomposition of \nabla u; restrict to hypersurface-orthogonal sector (vorticity =0).

What this buys. Local Lorentz is respected in all matter processes; any residual LV lives only in tiny curvature/strain effects (next-to-leading order, tunably small).

Idea. Treat u^\mu as a bona fide field but arrange the couplings so that:
